findings.title: No behavioral tests verify the 5,000 EUR daily transfer limit enforcement
findings.claim: The requirement specifies that the cumulative daily transfer limit check must enforce 5,000 EUR equivalent, allowing transfers at 5,000.00 and rejecting transfers at 5,000.01 or cumulative overruns. The test suite only asserts the property on BankSettings directly and does not test transfer limit enforcement behavior or boundary conditions.
findings.suggested_fix: Add integration/behavioral tests using the transfer service with BankSettings to assert that transfers up to 5,000 EUR equivalent succeed and transfers exceeding 5,000 EUR equivalent (including cumulative daily transfers) fail with daily limit validation errors.
findings.requirement_link: For any Customer initiating transfers, the cumulative daily transfer limit check enforces 5_000m EUR equivalent (using decimal arithmetic and Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero) where EUR equivalent conversion applies): a transfer causing the daily total to equal 5,000.00 EUR equivalent succeeds, while a transfer causing the daily total to exceed 5,000.00 EUR equivalent (e.g., 5,000.01 EUR equivalent or a second transfer pushing the UTC day total above 5,000.00) is rejected with the existing daily limit validation error and posts no ledger movement.

findings.title: Unsupported currency test catches generic Exception instead of specific domain exception
findings.claim: Customer_opening_account_with_unsupported_currency_is_rejected uses Assert.ThrowsAnyAsync<Exception>, which risks passing on unintended runtime faults such as NullReferenceException rather than validating business rule rejection.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace Assert.ThrowsAnyAsync<Exception> with Assert.ThrowsAsync<TException> specifying the exact exception type thrown for unsupported currency validation.
findings.requirement_link: When an authenticated Customer (or authorized role) creates a new account explicitly specifying another supported currency (such as "EUR" or "USD"), the account is still created in that requested supported currency.
